title: Identify Services from Other In-Scope AWS Service Categories

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Task Statement 3.8 collects services from categories that do not fit neatly into compute, networking, storage, databases, or analytics. Recognize the business need and match it to the service.
sections.callout: Recognize the business need → Match the service.

sections.title: Maestro Mental Model
sections.callout: INTEGRATE · COMMUNICATE · BUILD · DELIVER · PRESENT · CONNECT

entries.title: Amazon EventBridge
paragraphs: A serverless event bus that routes events from sources to configured targets using rules.

entries.title: Amazon SNS
paragraphs: A publish-and-subscribe service that broadcasts messages to multiple subscribers and notification endpoints.

entries.title: Amazon SQS
paragraphs: A managed message-queue service that buffers messages so producers and consumers can operate independently.
entries.memoryHook: Wait in line and process later.

sections.title: EventBridge vs. SNS vs. SQS

table.caption: Separate event routing, broadcasting, and queueing
rows: Publish one message to many subscribers
Hold messages until a consumer processes them

sections.callout: EVENT → EVENTBRIDGE · SHOUT → SNS · LINE → SQS

entries.title: Amazon Connect
paragraphs: A managed cloud contact-center service for customer communications.

entries.title: Amazon SES
paragraphs: Amazon Simple Email Service is a scalable service for sending and receiving transactional, marketing, and bulk email.

sections.title: AWS Support
paragraphs: AWS Support provides plans and resources that help customers operate and troubleshoot AWS environments. Support options differ in technical assistance, response targets, guidance, and added capabilities.
sections.callout: Business or technical assistance from AWS → AWS Support

sections.title: Customer Engagement and Assistance

entries.title: AWS Activate for Startups
paragraphs: Provides eligible startups with AWS credits, technical support, training, and business resources.

entries.title: AWS IQ
paragraphs: Connects customers with AWS Certified independent experts for project assistance.

entries.title: AWS Managed Services (AMS)
paragraphs: Provides ongoing AWS infrastructure operations and management using AWS practices and automation.

entries.title: AWS Support
paragraphs: Provides account and technical support options through support plans and AWS resources.
entries.memoryHook: AWS support for operating your environment.

sections.callout: STARTUP → ACTIVATE · PROJECT EXPERT → IQ · ONGOING OPERATIONS → AMS · SUPPORT CASE → AWS SUPPORT

sections.title: Developer Tools

entries.title: AWS AppConfig
paragraphs: Deploys and validates application configuration changes independently from application code deployments.

entries.title: AWS Cloud9
paragraphs: A cloud-based integrated development environment for writing, running, and debugging code.

entries.title: AWS CloudShell
paragraphs: A browser-based shell with AWS CLI access and credentials from the current console session.

entries.title: AWS CodeArtifact
paragraphs: Managed artifact repository for software packages used by development and build tools.

entries.title: AWS CodeBuild
paragraphs: A managed continuous-integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces deployable artifacts.

entries.title: AWS CodeCommit
paragraphs: Managed private Git repositories for source code.

entries.title: AWS CodeDeploy
paragraphs: Automates application deployments to supported compute targets.

entries.title: AWS CodePipeline
paragraphs: Models and automates build, test, approval, and deployment stages in a software release workflow.
entries.memoryHook: Move code through the delivery pipeline.

entries.title: AWS CodeStar
paragraphs: Provides a unified project experience for setting up and managing software-development projects with AWS developer tools.

entries.title: AWS X-Ray
paragraphs: Traces requests through distributed applications to identify errors, bottlenecks, and performance problems.

sections.callout: CONFIGURE · CODE · PACKAGE · BUILD · DEPLOY · PIPELINE · TRACE

entries.title: Amazon AppStream 2.0
paragraphs: Securely streams centrally managed desktop applications to users while the applications run remotely.

entries.title: Amazon WorkSpaces
paragraphs: Provides managed cloud-based virtual desktops that users access from supported devices.

entries.title: Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser
paragraphs: Provides isolated secure browser sessions for approved websites and web applications without a full virtual desktop.

table.caption: Choose the experience delivered to the user

entries.title: AWS Amplify
paragraphs: Provides tools and managed capabilities for developing, hosting, deploying, and connecting web and mobile application frontends.

entries.title: AWS AppSync
paragraphs: Provides managed GraphQL APIs and supports real-time and offline data synchronization for applications.

sections.title: IoT Services

entries.title: AWS IoT Core
paragraphs: Securely connects and manages Internet of Things devices, enabling device communication and message exchange with AWS services.

entries.title: AWS IoT Greengrass
paragraphs: Extends AWS capabilities to edge devices so they can process data and act locally, including during intermittent cloud connectivity.
entries.memoryHook: Run IoT logic at the edge.

sections.callout: CLOUD DEVICE CONNECTION → IOT CORE · LOCAL EDGE PROCESSING → IOT GREENGRASS

sections.title: GSA Scenario Recognition
bullets: Buffer messages for later processing → SQS
Ongoing infrastructure operations → AWS Managed Services
Provide secure browser access → WorkSpaces Secure Browser
Build and deploy a frontend → Amplify
Managed GraphQL API and real-time sync → AppSync
Run IoT logic at the edge → IoT Greengrass
sections.callout: Identify the business action before looking at service names.

entries.title: SNS vs. SQS
paragraphs: Broadcast → SNS. Queue → SQS.

entries.title: EventBridge vs. SNS
paragraphs: Event routing → EventBridge. Publish/subscribe notification → SNS.

entries.title: Connect vs. SES
paragraphs: Contact center → Connect. Email → SES.

entries.title: CodeBuild vs. CodePipeline vs. X-Ray
paragraphs: Build and test → CodeBuild. Automate delivery → CodePipeline. Trace and troubleshoot → X-Ray.

entries.title: CodeCommit vs. CodeArtifact
paragraphs: Store source code in Git repositories → CodeCommit. Store software packages → CodeArtifact.

entries.title: Cloud9 vs. CloudShell
paragraphs: Cloud development environment → Cloud9. Browser-based command shell → CloudShell.

entries.title: AppStream vs. WorkSpaces vs. Secure Browser
paragraphs: Stream an application → AppStream. Full virtual desktop → WorkSpaces. Isolated browser → WorkSpaces Secure Browser.

entries.title: Amplify vs. AppSync
paragraphs: Frontend development, hosting, and deployment → Amplify. Managed GraphQL APIs and real-time data synchronization → AppSync.

entries.title: Amplify vs. AppStream
paragraphs: Build or deploy a web/mobile frontend → Amplify. Stream an existing desktop application interface → AppStream.

entries.title: IoT Core vs. IoT Greengrass
paragraphs: Connect and manage devices through AWS → IoT Core. Process and act locally on edge devices → IoT Greengrass.
